issues.failure_explanation: Even granting the displayed error inequality, any signature containing a reversal has norm one. With identical shape parameters across intervals, C=1, while the sampled-data maximum Φ generally does not tend to zero as the mesh is refined. Thus the CΦ term persists even when h and the scaling factors tend to zero. The formal result supplies an error bound, not the claimed convergence argument; this gap remains independently of errors in deriving that bound.

failure_location.quote: Rigorous error analysis is presented to establish the convergence of the proposed zipper fractal interpolants to the underlying classical fractal functions, and subsequently, to the data-generating function.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State a refinement regime with uniformly bounded knot slopes and s=||λ||∞≤h/(t_n−t_1). Use the normalized basis weights and the contraction residual T_εψ−ψ to prove a bound of order ω_ψ(h)+hD+s. Applying this to both constructions establishes the two claimed limits.
issues.overall_effect: Convergence to the classical counterpart and to the generating function is not established for refinement sequences retaining nonzero signatures.
issues.title: The error estimate does not establish convergence for nonzero signatures
issues.why_classification: A contained new consistency estimate can establish convergence without excluding reversed signatures or changing the fixed-point construction.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: To guarantee the preservation of positivity, we derive sufficient conditions on the scaling coefficients $\lambda_j$ and the shape parameters $\alpha_{j,\epsilon}, \beta_{j,\epsilon}, \gamma_{j,\epsilon} \text{ and } \delta_{j,\epsilon}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem establishes only sufficient conditions, and its restrictions are not necessary. For constant positive data f_i=c, zero knot slopes, zero signature, and negative scaling factors satisfying |λ_j|<a_j, the displayed coefficients give M_j=(1−λ_j)c and the fixed point φ≡c. This positive interpolant violates the asserted nonnegative-scaling restriction.

failure_location.quote: We derive necessary constraints on the scaling factors and shape parameters to ensure positivity preservation.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the necessity claim by an explicit sufficiency claim and avoid presenting the admissible parameter region as necessary or exhaustive.
issues.overall_effect: The paper does not characterize necessary positivity restrictions; it supplies a sufficient parameter-selection rule.
issues.title: Sufficient positivity restrictions are advertised as necessary
issues.why_classification: This withdraws a substantive necessity assertion, but preserves the comparable, supported goal of sufficient positivity-preserving constraints.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For each subinterval, let $L_i : I \rightarrow I_i$ be a contraction mapping—typically affine—satisfying
L_i(t_1) = t_i, \quad L_i(t_n) = t_{i+1}, \quad \text{and} \quad |L_i(t) - L_i(t^*)| \leq \ell_i |t - t^*|, \quad \ell_i \in [0,1).

issues.failure_explanation: A contraction with these endpoints need not be injective. On I=[0,1], the piecewise-linear map through (0,0), (2/5,3/10), (3/5,1/5), and (1,1/2) maps onto [0,1/2], has Lipschitz constant 3/4, and satisfies the required endpoints, but is not injective. Its inverse is multivalued, so the stated operator is not defined.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require every L_i to be a homeomorphism onto I_i, or restrict to the affine maps actually used later.
issues.overall_effect: The operator and fixed-point assertion are unsupported for the full stated class of horizontal contractions.
issues.title: The FIF theorem uses inverses without requiring injective horizontal maps
issues.why_classification: A standard local hypothesis repairs the theorem while preserving the paper's affine interpolation construction and guarantees.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: F_i(t_1, f_1) = f_i, \quad F_i(t_n, f_n) = f_{i+1}.

issues.failure_explanation: The assumptions control only the second argument of F_i. Take knots 0,1/2,1, zero data, affine horizontal maps, F_1(t,f)=1 when t=1/2 and zero otherwise, and F_2=0. These maps satisfy the stated vertical contraction and endpoint conditions with λ_i=0, but every image under T has a discontinuous spike at 1/4. No continuous fixed point exists.

failure_location.quote: The IFS $\{W_i\}_{i=1}^{n-1}$ admits a unique attractor $G$, which coincides with the graph of a continuous function $h^* : I \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ that interpolates the given data, i.e., $h^*(t_j) = f_j$ for each $j$.

issues.why_classification: The missing continuity assumption is local and is already satisfied by the smooth auxiliary functions used in the proposed method.

issues.failure_explanation: The endpoint equations force a_j=−(t_{j+1}−t_j)/(t_n−t_1)<0 whenever ε_j=1. Consequently |λ_j|<a_j has no solution, including λ_j=0. The positivity theorem repeats the same signed-slope obstruction. Thus the declared parameter contract excludes every nonzero signature, including the all-one signatures used in the experiments.

issues.overall_effect: The advertised reversed-branch construction has an empty admissible parameter set, and its positivity prescription is unusable in that regime.

issues.why_classification: Separating signed slopes from contraction magnitudes is a local repair that restores the intended signature regime without changing the method or its intended rates.

In particular, repairing the scaling inequality to use |a_j| still does not make a reversed map satisfy the cited theorem's hypotheses. No applicable zipper C1 existence argument is supplied.

On the closed affine space of C1 functions with prescribed endpoint values and slopes, the displayed join-ups make the operator a self-map, and its C1 contraction factor is at most max_j{|λ_j|,|λ_j/a_j|}. This applies to the smooth trigonometric quotients when |λ_j|<|a_j|.

issues.failure_explanation: For a reversed branch, L_{j,ε}=L_{j,0}∘R with R(t)=t_1+t_n−t. At the same output point L_{j,ε}(t), the classical equation therefore contains φ(R(t)) and M_j(R(t)), not φ(t) and M_j(t). The subsequent use of a common signed slope in the derivative-coefficient differences also suppresses this orientation change.

With common shape parameters, e=||ε||∞, s=||λ||∞, D=max_i|d_i|, ΔF=max_j|f_{j+1}−f_j|, and B=F+2l max(|d_1|,|d_n|)/π, a valid replacement is e[ΔF+4hD/π+2s(||φ||∞+B)]/(1−s). issues.failure_explanation: For positive denominators, q_{j,ε}≤ξ implies 1/q_{j,ε}≥1/ξ, the opposite inequality from the one used. Thus replacing q_{j,ε} by its maximum can underestimate every positive summand. The resulting C=q_{j,ε}/ξ is not a valid uniform upper-bound coefficient; it can be made arbitrarily small by rescaling another interval's numerator and denominator without changing that interval's rational function.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Retain each actual denominator and use the normalized nonnegative weights, whose sum is one. Under β≥α and γ≥δ, also use αB_1+δB_2≤q. This removes the spurious ratio C and supplies genuine uniform coefficient bounds.
issues.overall_effect: The rational-term estimate and the resulting numerical error bound can be underestimates.

issues.why_classification: The available basis identities provide a short local repair affecting constants rather than the intended method, scope, or asymptotic form.

issues.failure_explanation: Taking the norm of a sum does not permit retaining a negative sign in front of the norm of one summand. Moreover, for ε_j=1 the two displayed derivative increments are opposites, so the corresponding contributions in the preceding expression add rather than produce the claimed subtraction. Signed slopes also require absolute values in a norm upper bound.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use positive absolute-value contributions with |a_j| and αB_1+δB_2. The normalized-weight estimate then bounds this contribution by 2h_j|d_{j+1}−d_j|/π, and hence by 4h_jD/π using a maximum over all knot slopes.
issues.overall_effect: The derivative contribution to the perturbation error is not bounded by the displayed expression and may be spuriously cancelled.
issues.title: The triangle-inequality estimate subtracts a norm
issues.why_classification: Correcting the local norm calculation preserves the stated order and requires no new construction or nontrivial lemma.

issues.failure_explanation: Both maxima omit the last knot, although the last branch uses f_n and d_n. For example, take zero scaling, zero slopes, all shape parameters one, f_1=⋯=f_{n−1}=0, f_n=1, and reverse the last branch. Its auxiliary-function difference has endpoint magnitude one, whereas Φ=η=0. Independently, for signed data an adjacent value difference is bounded by twice the full nodal maximum, not by that maximum alone.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use maxima over all n knots and the appropriate factor two for arbitrary signed data, or state the bound directly with max_j|f_{j+1}−f_j| and max_j|d_{j+1}−d_j|.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed data-dependent bound fails at the last interval and for general signed data allowed by the convergence theorem.
issues.title: The data-size quantities do not control the knot differences used in the proof
issues.why_classification: This is a local correction of the controlling quantities and constants, with no change to the construction or intended convergence order.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: It is observed that the shape parameters affect the shape of the RCTZFIF curve locally.

issues.failure_explanation: Let Δφ be the change between two fixed points. On any branch k whose parameters are unchanged, the functional equation gives Δφ(L_k(t))=λ_kΔφ(t), hence ||Δφ||_{I_k}=|λ_k| ||Δφ||_I. Therefore any nonzero perturbation propagates into every unchanged branch with nonzero scaling. The listed experiments have such branches. Only the direct modification of the defining maps is local; the resulting fractal interpolant is globally coupled.

failure_location.quote: We can observe from Figure \ref{fig:rctzfif_1c} that the effect of perturbation is local in subintervals.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the locality claim by the precise statement that changes act directly on selected branches and propagate as attenuated copies through other nonzero-scaling branches. State the displayed propagation relation instead of asserting confinement to the perturbed intervals.
issues.overall_effect: The examples do not establish strict local control by scaling or shape parameters in the nonzero-scaling fractal construction.
issues.title: Fractal parameter perturbations are incorrectly described as local
issues.why_classification: The advertised locality property must be weakened, but a comparable quantitative sensitivity description follows from the existing construction without changing it.
